subject: sociology

provenance.source: AglaSem Docs copy of the NTA master question paper (text in data/coverage/cuet2026/sociology-paper.json)
provenance.keySource: NTA CUET (UG) 2026 final answer key, option ids; all 50 questions authenticated by question id and option id

bankRead: One read-only snapshot on 22 Nov 2026 (tmp/1122-coverage/snap/sociology/bank_sociology.json, 280 visible rows). All 280 passed readablePracticeQuestions (eligible.txt), so served = 280 (served_rows.json, served_sociology.json). No database write.
keyCardDeck: data/keycards/decks/sociology.json (1,190 cards). The card suspension table was not read (no second production read); no card is known to be suspended.
syllabusSource: data/canonical_syllabus.js (14 sociology chapters); every question sits on the 2026 syllabus
method: data/coverage/METHOD.md (STRICT rule; doubtful = not covered; multi-statement and match items need every part). Facts written first in tmp/1122-coverage/work-sociology/facts_before_search.txt; searches with tmp/1122-coverage/work-sociology/ss.mjs; build script build_A.mjs there.
paperStructure: One section of 50 questions (501 to 550): 40 stand-alone MCQs, then two passages with 5 questions each (541-545 liberalisation, 546-550 mass media); all 50 are printed and counted as asked.
notes: Sociology has no numericals, so every covered verdict rests on a Key card or a bank key or explanation stating the fact.
Q41 to Q48 are comprehension items answerable from the printed passage: skill, shown, not counted. Q49 is also skill (the passage prints the defining sentence) although two cards teach the term.
Weakest covered calls, for Checker B to test first: Q8, Q14, Q22, Q40.
Q21: NTA key looks historically odd (Van Panchayats are older than the other events); it is not covered either way.

facts: Social demography (population studies) enquires into the wider causes and consequences of population structure and change; formal demography is the measurement of components

matches.teaches: Social demography enquires into the wider causes and consequences of population structures and change
Formal demography is quantitative; social demography looks at social, economic, political aspects

questions.reason: Key card gives the exact definition and the card for formal demography rules out the measurement option.

facts: Age structure = proportion of persons in different age groups relative to the total population

matches.teaches: Age structure is the proportion of persons in the different age groups relative to the total population
Bank explanation states age structure is the share of population in age groups

questions.reason: Key card states the definition word for word; the other options are the fertility rate, infant mortality rate and sex ratio, each defined by its own card.

facts: Industrialisation (an industrial town coming up in the midst of villages) physically transplants urban life into a rural setup
questions.reason: The only related material is the Rao card on the urban impact of an industrial town such as Bhilai; no served item states that industrialisation physically transplants urban life into a rural setup, so the match is doubtful.

facts: Universal adult suffrage was an outcome of a social movement in Britain
questions.reason: No served bank item or card mentions a British social movement or British suffrage; the cards on franchise are about the Karachi resolution and independent India.

facts: Caste is ascribed (determined by birth)
Caste groups are endogamous
Castes were traditionally linked to occupations, hereditary and not chosen (so a statement that caste rests on abilities and changes over time is false)

matches.teaches: Caste is determined by birth, endogamous, linked to hereditary occupations
Caste groups are endogamous
Within caste, birth dictates occupational opportunities

questions.reason: The six-features card states birth, endogamy and hereditary occupation, which settles A, B, C true and D false.

facts: Fertility rate = live births per 1000 women of child-bearing age
Infant mortality rate = deaths before age one per 1000 live births
Sex ratio = females per 1000 males
Dependency ratio = dependents compared with working-age group

matches.teaches: Fertility rate definition
Infant mortality rate definition
Sex ratio definition
Dependency ratio definition

questions.reason: Four Key cards give the four definitions the match list needs.

facts: Sanskritisation leads to adopting upper-caste practices such as dowry instead of bride-price, seclusion of women, discrimination against other groups

matches.teaches: Sanskritisation leads to dowry practices instead of bride-price
Sanskritisation: a lower group takes over upper-caste customs and style of life

questions.reason: Key card names dowry as an effect of sanskritisation; the other options are westernisation, occupational change and women working, which the card on westernisation separates.

facts: Tribes are classified on permanent traits (territory, language, physical features) and acquired traits (livelihood, extent of stratification and integration, i.e. assimilation into Hindu society)
Purity and pollution is the caste principle

matches.teaches: Permanent traits: region, language, physical features; acquired: livelihood and extent of assimilation into Hindu society
Acquired traits: livelihood, stratification, integration; language is permanent
Purity and pollution belongs to Hindu caste society

questions.reason: Two bank explanations list territory and language as permanent and assimilation into Hindu society as acquired; adopting the caste purity-pollution rule is that assimilation. Applying the fact takes one step, so this is the weakest of the covered.

facts: Lineage (matrilineal or patrilineal descent) determines rules of inheritance; residence, authority and marriage have their own rules

matches.teaches: Rules of inheritance differ with matrilineal and patrilineal descent
Matriliny is descent and inheritance through the female line
Residence is a separate rule
Authority is a separate rule

questions.reason: Card ties inheritance to the lineage type; residence and authority are separate cards, so the other options are ruled out.

facts: OBCs are a diverse group with regional variation
Two backward classes commissions (Kalelkar 1953, Mandal late 1970s) before 1990
Southern states had a long history of backward-caste agitation, earlier than the north
OBCs were low castes short of untouchability (service and artisanal), not untouchable

matches.teaches: OBCs are a much more diverse group
OBC issue became a regional affair at state level
First commission 1953
Second commission, Mandal
Southern states agitated from early twentieth century
OBCs were service and artisanal castes short of untouchability

questions.reason: Six Key cards state all four parts: diversity, two commissions, the south first, and not untouchable.

facts: Defenders of sati formed the Dharma Sabha against Roy and petitioned the British not to legislate: a counter movement defending the status quo

matches.teaches: Defenders of sati formed Dharma Sabha and petitioned the British not to legislate against sati
Counter movements arise in defence of the status quo

questions.reason: Key card is exactly this example of a counter movement.

facts: Language coupled with region and tribal identity, not religion, is the most powerful basis of ethno-national identity in India

matches.teaches: Language with regional and tribal identity, not religion, forms ethno-national identity

questions.reason: Key card names language, region and tribe and excludes religion, which gives A, C, D.

facts: Max Weber defined the state as a body that claims a monopoly of legitimate force in a territory

matches.teaches: Weber's definition of the state
Bank explanation: state has a monopoly of legitimate force

questions.reason: Key card is the quoted definition with its author.

facts: National unity in India rests on a recognition of differences
Inclusive nationalism was built into the Constitution (minority rights recognised in Articles 29 and 30)
The Indian state ruled out the assimilationist model; integration and assimilation assume a singular identity

matches.teaches: National unity is based upon a recognition of differences
Inclusive nationalism built into the Constitution
India ruled out an assimilationist model
Assimilation and integration assume a singular national identity

questions.reason: No single card states the sentence; four adjacent cards together teach it and rule out the assimilationist and singular-identity options. The second-weakest covered call.

facts: Bhopal (a princely-state city) lay outside the colonial economic system, while Bombay, Calcutta and Madras were colonial port cities
questions.reason: Cards say Bombay, Calcutta and Madras were colonial port cities, but nothing states which city stood outside the colonial economy; answering by elimination is not a taught fact.

facts: Urbanisation reorders relations between natives and migrants
Westernisation reorders social value systems
Modernisation = adopting new technology in production
Industrialisation reorders the market economy

matches.teaches: Only the native-immigrant relations part (Bhilai)

questions.reason: Only the urbanisation item is touched (Rao card, natives and immigrants); the westernisation, modernisation and industrialisation impacts as phrased in the list are not stated by any served item, and a match item needs every part.

facts: The 73rd Amendment gave a three-tier Panchayati Raj

matches.teaches: The 73rd Amendment provided a three-tier system of Panchayati Raj
73rd Amendment 1992 gave PRIs constitutional status

questions.reason: Key card states three tiers under the 73rd Amendment.

facts: Panchayats are delegated powers to prepare plans for economic development, promote social justice schemes, and levy taxes, duties, tolls and fees (not to make laws)

matches.teaches: Only the taxes part (sources of income)

questions.reason: Cards give Panchayat income and welfare functions; none states the delegated powers to plan economic development and social justice or that Panchayats do not make laws.

facts: Outsourcing: companies cut permanent staff and give work to smaller companies or to homes

matches.teaches: Companies reduce permanent employees and outsource work to smaller companies or homes
Small firms compete for orders from big companies

questions.reason: Key card is the same description with the term outsourcing as the answer.

facts: Article 21 (right to life and liberty) has been interpreted to include a life of quality: livelihood, health, shelter, education, dignity

matches.teaches: Article 21 interpreted as including all that goes into a life of quality

questions.reason: Key card states that judicial reading of the right to life covers quality of life.

facts: Order of: right to livelihood as part of Article 21, 73rd Amendment (1992), Van Panchayats, Right to Information Act

matches.teaches: Only the 1992 date

questions.reason: Only the 1992 amendment has a date; the dates of the right to livelihood ruling, the Van Panchayats and the RTI Act are not stated (the RTI card gives a 1993 court ruling only). NTA key also looks historically odd.

facts: India announced a population policy in 1952
Sex ratio fell to an all-time low of 927 (1991 census)
Population 121 crore in the 2011 census
India is younger than China around 2020 (average age 29 against 37)

matches.teaches: Official population policy announced in 1952
Sex ratio all-time low of 927 in 1991
Population 121 crores in the 2011 census
In 2020 average Indian 29 against China 37

questions.reason: Cards date the first three events (1952, 1991, 2011); the demographic-dividend event sits last by the 2020 average-age card. The fourth event is the weakest part; the order is still fixed.

facts: Famines tied to continuing poverty and malnutrition
Birth rate has not fallen as sharply as the death rate
Mass vaccination and sanitation helped control epidemics
Prosperity pulls family size down (so D is false)

matches.teaches: Mortality reduced, birth rate not brought down to the same extent
Prosperity pulls the birth rate down

questions.reason: B and D are stated, but the famine-and-poverty link and mass vaccination and sanitation are not (cards only say control over famines and epidemics); a multi-statement item needs every part.

facts: A state-nation lets various nations (ethnic, religious, linguistic identities) co-exist peacefully in one state polity; India is an example

matches.teaches: State nation: various nations co-exist peacefully in a single state polity
India is a good example of a state-nation

questions.reason: Key card gives the definition and names India as the example.

facts: The nationalist movement fought discrimination against lower castes yet protected upper-caste interests (the contradiction)

matches.teaches: Dominant nationalist view: caste a social evil and a colonial ploy

questions.reason: The card says nationalists saw caste as a social evil and a colonial ploy; it does not state the contradiction of serving upper-caste interests, so the key fact is missing.

facts: Anita Ghai is a leading scholar and activist on disability in India

matches.teaches: Anita Ghai is a leading activist and scholar of disability in India

questions.reason: Key card names her as a leading disability scholar.

facts: Communalism is aggressive chauvinism based on religious identity

matches.teaches: Communalism is aggressive chauvinism based on religious identity
Bank item states the same meaning

questions.reason: The scenario applies the definition; regionalism and casteism have their own cards.

facts: The jajmani system is a non-market exchange system

matches.teaches: Jajmani is a non-market exchange system

questions.reason: Key card names the jajmani system as the non-market example.

facts: An extended (joint) family has more than one couple, often over two generations, living together

matches.teaches: Extended family: more than one couple living together

questions.reason: Key card defines the extended family as more than one couple living together; nuclear, matrilocal and patrilocal are different ideas.

facts: The hundi was an instrument of exchange and credit (bill of exchange)

matches.teaches: Hundi: instrument of exchange and credit
Nakarattar is a banking system, not an instrument

questions.reason: Key card calls the hundi an instrument of exchange and credit.

facts: Population momentum = a large cohort of women of reproductive age fuels growth even with fewer children per woman

matches.teaches: Definition of population momentum
Bank item asks the term meaning, states continued growth from many people of reproductive age

questions.reason: Key card gives the description with the term as its answer.

facts: Marwaris succeeded in the colonial period using Calcutta
Marwaris moved from small traders to merchant bankers to industrialists
Their accumulated wealth did NOT have a negative impact on British commercial expansion (the false statement)

matches.teaches: Marwaris succeeded in colonial period in cities such as Calcutta
Small migrant traders to merchant bankers to industrialists

questions.reason: The three true statements are stated, but the effect of their wealth on British commercial expansion is not, so the false statement is found by elimination only; doubtful, counted as not covered.

facts: The Schedules listing castes and tribes were drawn up by the British Indian government in 1935 (legal recognition for special treatment)

matches.teaches: Schedules of castes and tribes drawn up in 1935 by the British Indian government

questions.reason: Key card states the 1935 schedules of castes and tribes recognised for special treatment.

facts: There is a close relationship between disability and poverty; disability is socially constructed

matches.teaches: Close relationship between disability and poverty
Disability creates and exacerbates poverty
Disability treated as socially constructed

questions.reason: Cards link disability with poverty, which is the social link the stem asks for.

facts: Apartheid in South Africa: protesters jailed and tortured, black wages a fraction of white wages, relocation to Bantustans; mixed marriages were banned (so B is false)
questions.reason: No served bank item or card mentions apartheid, Bantustans or South Africa.

facts: Prejudice = pre-conceived opinions towards another group
Stratification = categories of people ranked in a hierarchy
Exclusion = individuals cut off from full involvement in society
Discrimination = practices that disqualify one group from opportunities open to others

matches.teaches: Prejudice definition
Stratification: categories ranked in a hierarchy
Exclusion: cut off from full involvement
Discrimination: practices that disqualify members of one group from opportunities open to others

facts: Secularism, as the opposite of religious chauvinism, does not imply hostility to religion

matches.teaches: Secularism is the opposite of religious chauvinism and need not imply hostility to religion

questions.reason: Key card is the same sentence.

facts: Assimilation and integration policies aim at persuading or forcing all citizens to adopt a uniform set of cultural values and norms

matches.teaches: Assimilation aims at getting all citizens to adopt a uniform set of cultural values and norms
Integration insists on a common national public culture

questions.reason: Key cards state the uniform-norms aim of assimilation and the common public culture of integration.

facts: Civil society is the non-state and non-market part of the public domain where individuals voluntarily create institutions and organisations

matches.teaches: Civil society is the non-state, non-market part of the public domain with voluntary institutions

questions.reason: Key card is the same definition.

facts: Chipko = women and environmental concerns
Old social movements = reorganisation of power relations
Telangana = women and agrarian struggle
Dalit movement = space for self-determination

matches.teaches: Chipko concerns: economy, ecology, political representation
Large numbers of women hugged trees in Chipko
Old social movements saw reorganisation of power relations as central goal
Women took part in the Telangana arms struggle
Dalit movement: a space for self-determination

questions.reason: Cards cover each pair; the Chipko pair rests on two cards (women taking part, ecology concerns), the weakest link.

facts: Liberalisation = policies since 1991 (printed in the passage)
questions.reason: Answer is printed in the liberalisation passage (since July 1991); reading, not stored material.

facts: Liberalisation = removal of rules regulating trade and finance (printed in the passage)
questions.reason: Passage defines liberalisation as the steady removal of rules on trade and finance.

questions.reason: Passage says liberalisation opened the economy to the world market.

questions.reason: Passage lists the reforms across all major sectors.

questions.reason: Passage states that mass media work through very large organisations.

Gap between those with and without telecom and internet links

facts: The target audience of most soap operas is women
questions.reason: The passage does not print it; served cards on soaps (Hum Log, themes, urban consuming class) never state the target audience is women.
